item.title: ATP roundup: Stan Wawrinka has Swiss sendoff
item.description: Three-time Grand Slam winner Stan Wawrinka played the final match of his career Tuesday, falling 7-5, 7-6 (2) to eighth-seeded Czech Jiri Lehecka in the first round of the Swiss Indoors Basel in his native Switzerland.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Three-time Grand Slam winner Stan Wawrinka played the final match of his career Tuesday, falling 7-5, 7-6 (2) to eighth-seeded Czech Jiri Lehecka in the first round of the Swiss Indoors Basel in his native Switzerland. Wawrinka announced in December that 2026 would be his last season, and the ATP 500 event in Basel marked his final tournament. He received a tribute from the fans who came to watch their countryman compete one final time. Also in Basel, No. 1 seed Ben Shelton edged fellow American Aleksandar Kovacevic 6-7 (4), 7-6 (3), 7-6 (4). Shelton was credited with 44 aces and saved all four break points he faced in a match that lasted two hours, 38 minutes. No. 2 seed Arthur Fils eked past fellow Frenchman Giovanni Mpetshi Perricard 7-6 (5), 7-5, and Spanish third seed Rafael Jodar swept Chile's Alejandro Tabilo 6-4, 6-2. Other winners included No. 10 seed Hubert Hurkacz of Poland, Swiss wild card Jerome Kym and Alex Michelsen. Erste Bank Open No. 1 seed Alexander Zverev of Germany had to save four match points in the third-set tiebreaker to stave off Spanish wild card Martin Landaluce 7-5, 3-6, 7-6 (11) in first-round action in Vienna, Austria. Landaluce saved two match points in the 12th game of the deciding set to force the tiebreaker. Landaluce then went ahead at 6-5, 8-7, 9-8 and 10-9 only for Zverev to battle back each time. Zverev, the World No. 2, won 53 of 72 first-serve points (73.6%). No. 2 seed Carlos Alcaraz of Spain, playing in Vienna for the first time since 2021, defeated Russia's Karen Khachanov 6-4, 7-6 (5), with a 36-15 edge in winners. No. 4 seed Flavio Cobolli of Italy battled past Bulgarian wild card Grigor Dimitrov 6-4, 3-6, 6-3. No. 7 seed Tommy Paul, French qualifier Adrian Mannarino and Great Britain's Cameron Norrie also won their openers. --Field Level Media

item.title: Healey seeks to steer UK through 'difficult moment' with low-key budget
item.description: British finance minister John Healey is set to announce a cautious budget plan on Wednesday as he tries to avoid piling more bond market pressure on the new government of Prime Minister Andy Burnham.
item.dc:creator: William Schomberg
item.content:encoded: British finance minister John Healey is set to announce a cautious budget plan on Wednesday as he tries to avoid piling more bond market pressure on the new government of Prime Minister Andy Burnham. [USN:L8N4610PT TEXT:"Banks"], gambling firms and online marketplaces such as Amazon (AMZN.O) and Temu (PDD.O) are expected to be hit with higher taxes. That would help to pay for support for poorer households facing high energy bills and to freeze fuel duty for drivers. Healey – a [USN:L8N44P1EA TEXT:"former trade union official"] and a junior Treasury minister in the 1990s – says he wants to give Britain "a bit of breathing space" from the impact of the US-led war on Iran that is pushing up inflation. "This budget is about getting through this difficult moment. But it's also about putting Britain on a future path, a better future path," he said in a statement. DEVOLUTION, DEFENCE AND DEBT His first budget – due to be announced in parliament just after 12:30 p.m. (1230 GMT) – will detail how the government plans to give regional mayors more control over tax revenues, part of Burnham's [USN:L8N4691W8 TEXT:"devolution push"]. Separately, more than [USN:L6N46A01K TEXT:"£20 billion"] in extra support will go to state finance institutions to spur investment in artificial intelligence, defence and green energy by the early 2030s. On entering Downing Street in July, Burnham promised "the biggest changes in the last 40 years", including a bigger role for the state in the economy. But Healey's options are limited by the surge in borrowing costs for governments around the world including Britain, where investors remember the 2022 "mini-budget" of former Prime Minister Liz Truss and the ensuing bond market meltdown triggered by its unfunded tax cuts. On Tuesday, Britain paid the [USN:L5N46D0XF TEXT:"highest interest"] on a 5-year government bond since 2008. After big tax and spending increases in the two budgets of the previous finance minister Rachel Reeves, Wednesday is being framed as a "steady as she goes" moment for Britain's economy, which has so far withstood the Iran war energy price shock. Bond dealers [USN:L8N4682G5 TEXT:"polled by Reuters"] expect less than £10 billion in extra debt issuance this financial year, compared with April's forecasts, though they see financing needs for next year being revised up by more than £25 billion. In an attempt to ease some of Reeves' big tax hit on employers, Healey has said he would [USN:L8N4682B4 TEXT:"reduce paperwork"] for businesses to save them £800 million a year. Bigger policy changes – including how to fix the inflation hit to public spending – are likely to have to wait for a 10-year plan that Burnham has said he will announce later this year and a broad spending review in 2027. But Healey is under pressure to say now how he intends to pay more for [USN:L5N46C0B7 TEXT:"defence"] – an issue that caused him to quit as defence minister in June in a move that hastened Keir Starmer's resignation as prime minister. Possible savings from reforms to Britain's fast-growing welfare spending could offer a bit of latitude later this year. But Healey's biggest hope is for an end to the Iran war, which would lower the government's bill for servicing £3 trillion of public debt. That was already on course to gobble up more than 10% of public spending before the war began. He has said he would stick to the government's fiscal targets, key for maintaining the confidence of the bond market. Britain's budget forecasters are expected to say on Wednesday that the margin for meeting the more challenging target has fallen to £15 billion, from £24 billion in March. The Treasury has announced a string of low-cost policies to try to show it can still help voters, including tariff cuts on some imported goods including gherkins and marmalade. Sarah Coles, head of personal finance at investment platform AJ Bell, said targeted tax changes could help carers and parents. "For others they will be a drop in the ocean. Hard-pressed households will be hoping for more support," Coles said.

item.title: Movida tem salto no lucro líquido do 3º tri para R$152,1
item.description: A Movida Participações anunciou que teve lucro líquido de R$152,1 milhões no terceiro trimestre, salto de 117% em relação ao mesmo período um ano antes e superando seu guidance, segundo balanço divulgado nesta terça-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Movida Participações (MOVI3.SA) anunciou que teve lucro líquido de R$152,1 milhões no terceiro trimestre, salto de 117% em relação ao mesmo período um ano antes e superando seu guidance, segundo balanço divulgado nesta terça-feira. A empresa de aluguel de veículos, gestão de frotas e venda de seminovos teve resultado operacional medido pelo lucro antes de juros, impostos, depreciação e amortização (Ebitda) de R$1,79 bilhão, expansão de 21,4% na base anual. A receita líquida do grupo foi de R$3,87 bilhões no período, crescimento de 2,8% em relação ao terceiro trimestre de 2025, com a margem EBITDA de locação atingindo recorde de 74,2% no trimestre, avanço de 1,6 p.p. em relação ao mesmo trimestre de 2025. "Os resultados também foram beneficiados pelas iniciativas de verticalização da manutenção, com destaque para a expansão da rede de Pit Stops e dos Centros de Preparação, que vêm contribuindo para a redução de custos, aumento da produtividade e fortalecimento da qualidade dos serviços prestados", disse a empresa no comunicado.

item.title: Canada's Wealthsimple raises funds at C$13.80 billion valuation
item.description: Canadian financial services company Wealthsimple said on Tuesday it had raised up to C$425 million ($302.5 million), taking its valuation to C$13.8 billion as it expands its challenge to the country's dominant banks.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Canadian financial services company Wealthsimple said on Tuesday it had raised up to C$425 million ($302.5 million), taking its valuation to C$13.8 billion as it expands its challenge to the country's dominant banks. Here are some details: "We're seeing tremendous momentum from Canadians that are choosing to leave the banks and live their entire financial lives on Wealthsimple. And we don't want to slow down. We want to speed up and keep launching new products," CEO Michael Katchen said in an interview with Reuters Canada's six biggest banks, including Royal Bank of Canada (RY.TO) and Toronto-Dominion Bank (TD.TO) , control most of the banking sector Meanwhile, digital challengers such as Wealthsimple, which had C$169.2 billion in assets under administration as of September 30, have been attracting younger customers The fundraise values Toronto-based Wealthsimple at C$13.8 billion, nearly [USN:L4N3W81PP TEXT:"40% higher"] than the C$10 billion valuation it secured in 2025 On IPO plans, Katchen said the company was "not in a rush," but that public markets were "certainly ... the destination" This round was led by Singapore sovereign wealth fund GIC, with participation from existing investors Power Corporation of Canada (POW.TO) , IGM Financial (IGM.TO) , ICONIQ, CPP Investments and Inovia Wealthsimple said it would use the proceeds to develop new products and expand its banking and investment services ($1 = 1.4049 Canadian dollars)

item.title: SK Hynix unveils shareholder return plan worth $75 billion after posting 7-fold jump in Q3 profit
item.description: South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix reported a more than seven-fold rise in quarterly operating profit to a record high on Wednesday, beating market forecasts, as continued demand for AI infrastructure drove up memory chip prices.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix (000660.KS) reported a more than seven-fold rise in quarterly operating profit to a record high on Wednesday, beating market forecasts, as continued demand for AI infrastructure drove up memory chip prices. The Nvidia (NVDA.O) supplier also said it will pursue shareholder returns totalling about 100 trillion won ($75.4 billion) this year, comprising cash dividends of 30 trillion won and share repurchases and cancellations of 60 trillion won, including 40 trillion won announced in August. SK Hynix also reiterated that it expects demand to continue to exceed supply through 2030. To improve mid-to-long term demand visibility, SK Hynix has signed long-term agreements (LTAs) with 14 major customers, while "proactively discussing with a number of customers the possibility of extending the contract terms, which are typically five years." "The LTA volume secured to date corresponds to more than 50% of total production capacity for 2027 and 2028," SK Hynix said. SK Hynix reported operating profit of 83.3 trillion won for the July-September period, compared with 11.4 trillion won a year earlier. That compared with the 76.7 trillion won LSEG SmartEstimate, which is weighted toward estimates from analysts who are more consistently accurate. Quarterly revenue rose 328% to 104.6 trillion won. SK Hynix shares rose 2% in line with the wider market's (.KS11) 2.2% gain. ($1 = 1,326.0900 won)

item.title: Report: Wolves star Anthony Edwards (knee) out up to 2 months
item.description: The Minnesota Timberwolves will be without superstar guard Anthony Edwards for up to two months after he undergoes arthroscopic surgery on his right knee, ESPN reported Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Minnesota Timberwolves will be without superstar guard Anthony Edwards for up to two months after he undergoes arthroscopic surgery on his right knee, ESPN reported Tuesday. Edwards, 25, played through soreness and inflammation in his right knee during the 2025-26 regular season and postseason before suffering a left knee hyperextension and bone bruise in the first round of the playoffs. The four-time All-Star took about two months off over the summer to rest and allow his knees to heal without surgery. A two-time All-NBA Second Team selection, Edwards is coming off a 47-point performance Monday in a loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers. It marked the seventh time in his career he has scored at least 47 points. Through four games this season, Edwards is averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds and 3.5 assists while shooting 48.1% from the field and 40.0% from 3-point range for the Timberwolves (3-1). The No. 1 overall pick in the 2020 NBA Draft, Edwards is in his seventh season with Minnesota and has career averages of 24.6 points, 5.2 rebounds and 4.1 assists in 446 games (427 starts). He has made 1,332 3-pointers at a 37% clip. Minnesota hosts the Golden State Warriors on Wednesday night. --Field Level Media

item.title: First Venezuelan oil from US-NABEP deal arrives in Texas, to be sold to Exxon, Citgo
item.description: The first cargo of Venezuelan crude under a deal between the US and producer NABEP unloaded in Texas on Tuesday and will be sold by the US government to refineries run by Exxon Mobil and Venezuelan-owned Citgo Petroleum, a White House official said.
item.dc:creator: Jarrett Renshaw
item.content:encoded: The first cargo of Venezuelan crude under a deal between the US and producer NABEP unloaded in Texas on Tuesday and will be sold by the US government to refineries run by Exxon Mobil (XOM.N) and Venezuelan-owned Citgo Petroleum, a White House official said. NABEP confirmed in a statement it supplied 1 million barrels of Venezuelan oil as part of the deal. President Donald Trump visited the port on Tuesday, where one of the vessels carrying the heavy crude served as a backdrop for his speech. The government received the oil "at no cost," the White House official told Reuters, while Trump called it a gift earlier in the day. NABEP's statement, which initially characterized the shipment as part of Washington's right to buy 20% of production at cost with no markup, was later updated to say the cargo came at no cost to US taxpayers "to recognize the historic nature of the agreement." "They've sent me as a gift a boatload of a million barrels of oil, and I'm giving that to the United States of America,” Trump told reporters. He later called it the "first shipment of BILLIONS of Barrels to come" in a post on Truth Social. The delivery is the first from an arrangement that gives Washington a 35% stake in NABEP's parent company and discounted access to crude it produces. The pact, struck after US forces captured and removed former President Nicolas Maduro from power in January, handed NABEP 14 additional oilfields on top of the three it already had in Venezuela, without a competitive process. "This first shipment since the US-NABEP deal will be followed by thousands of such arrivals," NABEP CEO Alejandro Betancourt said in the company's statement. He said the cargo reached Texas in just over a week, compared with more than a month for crude from the Middle East. OUTPUT RISING IN VENEZUELA NABEP has said the 17 fields it controls in Venezuela hold an estimated 65 billion barrels of oil reserves. The company's total output reached 223,509 barrels of oil equivalent per day as of October 19, it said, up from about 18,000 bpd two years ago. Betancourt said last week that output at Petrozamora, its largest active project, had risen to 115,000 bpd. The shipment gives Trump a chance to tout access to cheaper crude as evidence his policies are delivering economic benefits ahead of the [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"], with fuel costs a potential vulnerability for Republicans. In Texas, Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton faces Democrat James Talarico in a [USN:L1N45T11E TEXT:"closely watched race"] that could help determine control of the Senate. "We're celebrating the greatest oil victory in history. To the victor belongs the spoils, right?" Trump said. Trump also praised oil executive Harold Hamm, who was in attendance, as the "biggest independent oilman in the world," before recounting a conversation about Venezuela's vast petroleum reserves. Hamm had described the country's oil wealth as so abundant that finding it was almost effortless, Trump said. "You know how you find oil in Venezuela? You look on the ground. There it is," Trump said.

item.title: Alabama DB Dre Kirkpatrick Jr. dismissed from team after arrest
item.description: Alabama defensive back Dre Kirkpatrick Jr. was dismissed from the program on Tuesday, one day after he was charged with misdemeanors alleging he doxed and harassed a university police officer.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Alabama defensive back Dre Kirkpatrick Jr. was dismissed from the program on Tuesday, one day after he was charged with misdemeanors alleging he doxed and harassed a university police officer. "After gathering more information on the situation, Dre Kirkpatrick Jr. will no longer be a part of our program," Alabama coach Kalen DeBoer said in a statement. "He did not live up to the standards and expectations that I have set for this team and our players." The Athletic reported that Kirkpatrick was charged almost a year after his November 2025 arrest on three counts of reckless endangerment, attempting to elude and speeding after a traffic stop on the Tuscaloosa Strip. Kirkpatrick was arrested Friday and then charged Monday in Tuscaloosa County District Court. Prosecutors allege Kirkpatrick sent the officer, who conducted the 2025 traffic stop, a profanity-laced Facebook Messenger message on Oct. 20 and posted a photo of the officer, his wife and their two children on his own Facebook page with the caption "Dis him?", according to court records obtained by The Athletic. The officer told investigators that he was concerned for his safety and that of his family. The 20-year-old junior from Gadsden, Ala., did not play Saturday after being designated as out on the SEC availability report prior to the Crimson Tide's 31-20 win over Texas A&M. DeBoer said Monday during an appearance at the Monday Morning Quarterback Club in Birmingham, Ala., that Kirkpatrick had been suspended. After his arrest last November, Kirkpatrick was suspended for the final seven games of the season. He finished his second season in the program with nine tackles and a forced fumble in eight games. He appeared in the Crimson Tide's first seven games this season, totaling five tackles, one forced fumble and one pass breakup. No. 10 Alabama has a bye this weekend before playing at rival No. 15 LSU on Nov. 7. Kirkpatrick is the son of former Alabama and NFL defensive back Dre Kirkpatrick, who played eight of his 10 seasons with the Cincinnati Bengals. --Field Level Media

item.title: FBI agent says he feared case against ex-FBI officials tied to Hunter Biden probes would look political
item.description: An FBI agent who helped lead the case against two former senior bureau officials accused of lying to Congress about Hunter Biden investigations testified on Tuesday that he feared the probe would look "political".
item.dc:creator: Andrew Goudsward
item.content:encoded: An FBI agent who helped lead the case against two former senior bureau officials accused of lying to Congress about Hunter Biden investigations testified on Tuesday that he feared the probe would look "political". The testimony came at a hearing to decide whether the [USN:L6N4690Z1 TEXT:"case"] against Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, both former senior counterintelligence officials, can go forward. It adds to defense claims that the Trump Justice Department brought the case for political reasons, which prosecutors deny. FBI special agent Bryan Witt said his concerns were based on the fact that the probe began in July, the day after President Donald Trump gave a[USN:L1N43H131 TEXT:" primetime speech"] in which he directed the FBI and other agencies to investigate whether the US intelligence community suppressed information about foreign meddling in the 2020 election. One of the former FBI officials who was charged, Nikki Floris, sought to discredit an FBI intelligence report that said China sought to influence the 2020 election in favor of Biden. FBI Director Kash Patel directed the FBI’s field office in Kansas City, Missouri, where Witt is based, to investigate following Trump’s address, Witt testified. “I had concerns this would be viewed as political,” Witt said. The testimony revealed concerns within the FBI about a probe into two of the FBI’s most senior counterintelligence officials whose actions Trump and Republican lawmakers had condemned for years. The case is the latest brought by the Trump Justice Department to face claims of political bias. Justice Department officials have argued the former FBI officials should be held accountable for misleading a congressional investigation. Spokespeople for the Justice Department and FBI did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Prosecutors called Witt to testify as the agent who outlined the allegations in a criminal complaint. Asked by Floris’ defense lawyer, Margaret Donovan, if he viewed the investigation as a “witch hunt,” Witt denied making that statement but said “people generally viewed it as that around the office.” The direction of the probe eventually changed from foreign election influence to 2023 testimony by Floris and Benavides before the House of Representatives Judiciary Committee. Both were charged last week with making false statements about their knowledge and involvement in Hunter Biden investigations. Hunter Biden was charged during his father's administration with tax and gun crimes. Former President Joe Biden pardoned his son shortly before leaving office. Floris and Benavides were both supervisors on the FBI’s foreign influence task force ahead of the 2020 election. A criminal complaint accused them of lying to the House panel in denying or downplaying their role in Hunter Biden probes, citing internal FBI records and witness interviews. JUDGE CRITICIZES PROSECUTORS Attorneys for Floris and Benavides have disputed the allegations and accused the Trump administration of bringing the case to drive a political narrative. US Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui, who presided over the hearing, said their claims had some credibility as he condemned prosecutors for filing a new criminal complaint early on Tuesday that added an obstruction charge against both defendants without seeking a judge’s approval. Faruqui said he was aware of no previous instance of prosecutors filing a criminal complaint that had not been approved by a magistrate judge. Prosecutors denied doing anything improper and argued they were not legally required to seek a judge’s sign-off. Faruqui told prosecutors their conduct bolstered defense claims that “everything here is atypical and bizarre and that is because this is not an appropriate case.”

item.title: Colts keep dealing, trade DT DeForest Buckner back to 49ers
item.description: The Indianapolis Colts sent three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the team that drafted him, the San Francisco 49ers, in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round pick, ESPN and NFL Network reported Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Indianapolis Colts sent three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the team that drafted him, the San Francisco 49ers, in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round pick, ESPN and NFL Network reported Tuesday. The move comes on the same day the Colts traded another major player to an NFC West team in eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson, 30, who was traded to the Seattle Seahawks earlier Tuesday in exchange for a 2027 third-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round selection. That deal is pending a physical exam. Buckner's four sacks this season ties Adetomiwa Adebawore for most on the Colts but is more than any Niners player this season. In San Francisco, the 32-year-old will start alongside Osa Odighizuwa at tackle and aim to help an injury-ravaged defensive line that has played much of this season without end Nick Bosa (calf) and Sam Okuayinonu (foot) and tackles Alfred Collins (patellar tendon), C.J. West (knee) and James Thompson Jr. (ankle). Despite the injuries, the 49ers stand at 6-1, while the Colts have struggled to a 2-5 record, prompting visible frustration from Buckner after Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. When asked by reporters for his reaction to the team's recent struggles, he snapped, "I don't know. How about you guess. I'm frustrated. Same thing. We lost," and when asked what needed to change, he said, "I don't know. I can't tell you." Buckner previously signed multiple contract extensions to stay in Indianapolis despite late-season collapses. He is entering the final year of his latest deal with the Colts and is set to become an unrestricted free agent after the season. Buckner has 75.5 sacks, 11 fumble recoveries and 683 tackles in 158 games (153 starts) with San Francisco (2016-19) and Indianapolis. The 49ers drafted him with the No. 7 overall pick in 2016, and San Francisco general manager John Lynch called trading Buckner to the Colts in 2020 "the toughest thing I've done since I've been a general manager here." --Field Level Media

item.title: Hegseth likely to face questions on US role in Indo-Pacific at ASEAN summit
item.description: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is likely to face questions about Washington’s commitment to the Indo-Pacific region when he meets Southeast Asian counterparts in the Philippines on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Karen Lema
item.content:encoded: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is likely to face questions about Washington’s commitment to the Indo-Pacific region when he meets Southeast Asian counterparts in the Philippines on Wednesday. As the Iran war strains US military readiness and tension rises with China, the Pentagon said Hegseth's attendance at the gathering in the Philippine province of Cebu would reaffirm Washington’s commitment to "peace through strength" in the Pacific. Analysts said Southeast Asian nations could use meetings with Hegseth on the sidelines to seek clarity about the endgame in Iran, US expectations from allies and partners, and how the conflict's demands square with commitments to the Indo-Pacific. "They will want to seek answers from the United States regarding certainty towards alliances and partnerships," said Collin Koh, a security scholar at Singapore's S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies. "And of course, the bigger elephant in the room is how does that juxtapose with US commitment to the Indo-Pacific or Western Pacific theatre." ECONOMIES GRAPPLING WITH IRAN WAR IMPACT Southeast Asian economies are grappling with the effects of Iran war, while tension between host the Philippines and Beijing add another source of friction to a forum meant to promote dialogue and practical cooperation on security. The Iran war , launched by US and Israeli strikes on February 28, has disrupted shipping and oil markets, exposing Southeast Asia’s vulnerability to imported-fuel shocks and pushing energy security higher on ASEAN's agenda. Greg Poling, director of the Asia Maritime Transparency Initiative said Hegseth would get an opportunity at the gathering to tackle aspects regarding China, the disputed South China Sea and Washington’s commitments to its treaty allies. "Most will want reassurance about U.S. commitment to the region, despite the political turmoil in Washington and the weakening of both U.S. capabilities and readiness by the war in Iran." The topic is critical for the Philippines, a US treaty ally whose ties with Beijing have soured amid repeated confrontations in the disputed South China Sea, Chinese [USN:P8N3VV02G TEXT:"sanctions"] and, more recently, a [USN:L1N46508J TEXT:"summoning"] of the Chinese ambassador. China's defence attaché in the Philippines will attend the meeting, its defence ministry said on Tuesday. Days before the meeting, set for October 28 and 29, the Philippine military said it monitored and shadowed China's Liaoning aircraft carrier group as it passed through waters off the southern Philippines toward the Celebes Sea. Stronger signals were more likely to figure in talks among like-minded partners, added Poling. Such partners include the Squad, a grouping of the United States, Japan, Australia and the Philippines, whose defence chiefs are set to meet on October 28. EVENTUAL CHAIRMAN'S STATEMENT SEEN AS RESTRAINED However, the eventual chairman's statement was likely to be more restrained than talks behind closed doors and would employ familiar ASEAN language, said Koh. Manila’s position as ASEAN chair while embroiled in a dispute with China was "particularly sensitive", he added. Poling said the Philippines had to balance "aspirational cooperation" on issues such as energy connectivity, the digital economy and coast guard cooperation against rising tension with China and stalled progress on a South China Sea code of conduct. "For the Philippines, the whole ASEAN chair year has been a difficult balance," added Poling, who is also a fellow with the Southeast Asia Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies. "I’d expect tactical cooperation on the ADMM workstreams ... but no strategic alignment on the South China Sea or other thorny issues," he said, referring to the bloc's effort to tackle issues such as maritime security and counter-terrorism.

item.title: From Formula One outsider to 300 starts: Perez marks milestone in Mexico
item.description: Sergio "Checo" Perez will make his 300th Formula One start in front of his home fans in Mexico City, capping a career that began with a teenage move to Europe and grew alongside the sport's resurgence in his country.
item.dc:creator: Angelica Medina
item.content:encoded: Sergio "Checo" Perez will make his 300th Formula One start in front of his home fans in Mexico City, capping a career that began with a teenage move to Europe and grew alongside the sport's resurgence in his country. "Honestly, not even in my wildest dreams could I have imagined it," Perez told reporters on Tuesday about reaching the milestone at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez. Perez's landmark start was moved to his home race by a reshaped calendar after the cancellations of the Saudi Arabian and Bahrain Grands Prix, with Malaysia replacing Bahrain. "Reaching so many Grands Prix will be an unforgettable moment, one that makes me very proud of my career and of the professionalism I have had". The 35-year-old has spent more than 15 years in Formula One, having raced for Sauber, McLaren, Force India, Racing Point and Red Bull, before joining Cadillac's new project. His career highlights include his first Formula One victory in Bahrain in 2020, a Monaco Grand Prix win in 2022 and a home podium in Mexico, which he ranked as his most special moment. Formula One returned to Mexico in 2015, after a 23-year absence, giving Perez the chance to race at home for the first time since his karting days. "Once the Mexican Grand Prix began, the sport grew enormously in our country. Before that people did not really talk about motorsport; it felt very distant," Perez added saying the race return help turn the country into one of the sport's most passionate stops. "For me, it became the best Grand Prix in Formula 1," he said. Perez's 300th start follows a season away from the grid, a period he said changed his outlook on the intensity and scrutiny of Formula One. "When I stepped away from Formula 1, I realised that not every single moment is that important," Perez said. "What matters is staying balanced, not feeling too high in the good moments and not feeling too low in the bad ones." At Cadillac, Perez said he faces a new kind of challenge as the team looks to establish itself in Formula One. "This is my greatest challenge and my biggest objective: to take Cadillac forward," he said. "We started from the back, and I want to see how far we can go over the coming years." Perez said he wanted to decide for himself when to leave Formula One and to do so while still performing at a high level. "As an athlete, it is very important to me to finish my career on a high note, to leave Formula 1 when I decide to leave, and while still performing at a high level." He added he remained focused on driving rather than a future management role. "When my time as a driver ends, I have always said that I am excited about exploring other areas and learning other things."

item.title: Alexander brothers get 30 years each in prison after sex trafficking convictions
item.description: Three brothers convicted of exploiting their access to wealth and high society in New York and Miami to drug and rape women were each sentenced on Tuesday to 30 years in prison.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Three brothers convicted of exploiting their access to wealth and high society in New York and Miami to drug and rape women were each sentenced on Tuesday to 30 years in prison. The twins Alon Alexander and Oren Alexander, 39, and Tal Alexander, 40, were sentenced by US District Judge Valerie Caproni in Manhattan, seven months after being convicted in a six-week trial of multiple sex crimes including conspiracy to commit sex trafficking. Lawyers for the brothers did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Caproni called the brothers' conduct "monstrous," according to multiple media reports. Oren and Tal Alexander were co-founders of the luxury real estate brokerage Official, while Alon Alexander was an executive at his family's security company Kent Security. Prosecutors sought life sentences, while the Alexanders requested mandatory minimum 15-year prison terms. Prosecutors said the brothers for at least 14 years exploited their social status to prey on women and girls, with more than 70 women saying they were assaulted by one or more of the brothers in locations including Manhattan, the Hamptons on New York's Long Island, and Aspen, Colorado. In one instance, prosecutors said in January 2017 three girls were celebrating their senior year in high school at an Aspen nightclub when the brothers drugged them, enticed them to their five-star hotel for a promised after party, and then assaulted them. New York City Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said in a statement provided by the US Attorney's office in Manhattan, which prosecuted the Alexanders: "With today's sentencing, they will finally face the consequences they deserve for the incredible harm they inflicted on so many."

item.title: Thousands rally outside Portugal's parliament over housing crisis, police operations
item.description: Thousands rallied outside Portugal's parliament in Lisbon on Tuesday to protest against a deepening housing crisis and recent police operations against housing activists, while lawmakers debated the government's draft budget for 2027.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Goncalves, Miguel Pereira
item.content:encoded: Thousands rallied outside Portugal's parliament in Lisbon on Tuesday to protest against a deepening housing crisis and recent police operations against housing activists, while lawmakers debated the government's draft budget for 2027. Portugal faces one of Europe's most acute home affordability crises, with prices more than doubling since 2017 and new-lease rents nearly doubling, hitting young people hardest, as wages have not kept up. Tuesday's protest followed baton-charging police operations to [USN:L2N46B014 TEXT:"dismantle tent camps"] set up by housing activists in Lisbon and Porto on Sunday, sparking allegations of excessive force. Rally organisers said several thousand people packed the area. Police gave no crowd estimate. The Portuguese protests echo recent demonstrations in [USN:L1N45U0F8 TEXT:"Spain"] and elsewhere across Europe over housing shortages and surging rents. Erica Rodrigues, 39, an actress, said the crisis affects young people and older generations because the "cost of living in Portugal is very high for what people earn. It is unbearable." "My congratulations to this government for the clown show it has put on in recent times. It has done a terrible job," she said. Protesters demanded the minority centre-right government scrap a [USN:L6N45M1AX TEXT:"bill"] that would speed up evictions and end rent caps on new leases, which passed a first reading with the far-right Chega party abstaining. Joao Martins, 39, unemployed, said protesters were "fighting for decent and affordable housing for everyone" and for a "state budget that genuinely reflects the interests of the majority of the population, rather than just a few privileged people". He said they were also demonstrating "for the right to protest, which has been seriously threatened in recent days". Portugal's internal affairs watchdog, the IGAI, opened an inquiry into the police operations, while prosecutors launched a separate investigation into officers' conduct. Police reported 11 minor injuries, including 3 officers, in the two operations on Sunday, while activist group Casa para Viver (Homes to Live) said 60 were hurt. Speaking in parliament on Tuesday, Prime Minister Luis Montenegro said police acted in line with the principles of "necessity, proportionality and adequacy".

item.title: Australia’s PLS signs 20-year power deal with Fortescue unit for Pilgangoora lithium mine
item.description: Australia's PLS Group signed a 20-year power purchase agreement with FMG Clean Energy on Wednesday, owned by iron ore miner Fortescue , to meet growing power demand at its Pilgangoora operation under the P2000 expansion plan.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Australia's PLS Group (PLS.AX) signed a 20-year power purchase agreement with FMG Clean Energy on Wednesday, owned by iron ore miner Fortescue (FMG.AX) , to meet growing power demand at its Pilgangoora operation under the P2000 expansion plan. The country's largest independent lithium producer plans to invest about A$150 million ($105.42 million) between 2027 and 2029 in transmission connection and power infrastructure upgrades. FMG will supply at least 325 gigawatt-hours of electricity annually to the Pilgangoora Operation from 2029, subject to regulatory approvals and construction of the required infrastructure. PLS expects the agreement to lower unit operating costs at Pilgangoora by about A$15 to A$20 per tonne under its P2000 expansion plan. "PLS is our first customer, with a strong pipeline of others across the Pilbara looking to our Green Grid for greater choice and flexibility in how they source their power," said Fortescue CEO, Dino Otranto. The company expects the agreement to help cut Pilgangoora's power-related emissions intensity to reduce by up to 80% from 2023 levels by 2030. Separately, PLS revised its full-year capital expenditure forecast for 2027 to A$1.13 to $1.20 billion, up from its previous outlook of A$1.11 to A$1.18 million. Earlier this month, PLS had [USN:L4N461284 TEXT:"approved"] a A$1.9 billion expansion of Pilgangoora lithium mine, betting that growing electric-vehicle adoption would support long-term lithium demand despite recent price volatility. ($1 = 1.4229 Australian dollars)

item.title: Hypera tem lucro de R$527 mi no 3º tri
item.description: A farmacêutica Hypera teve lucro líquido de R$527 milhões no terceiro trimestre, crescimento de 16,1% sobre o resultado obtido no mesmo período do ano passado, segundo balanço divulgado nesta terça-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A farmacêutica Hypera (HYPE3.SA) teve lucro líquido de R$527 milhões no terceiro trimestre, crescimento de 16,1% sobre o resultado obtido no mesmo período do ano passado, segundo balanço divulgado nesta terça-feira. A companhia apurou um resultado operacional medido pelo lucro antes de juros, impostos, depreciação e amortização (Ebitda) 3,4% maior na mesma comparação, a R$782,3 milhões. Analistas, em média, esperavam que a Hypera divulgasse lucro líquido de R$471,4 milhões no terceiro trimestre e Ebitda de R$772 milhões, segundo dados da LSEG. A empresa, que é dona de marcas como Neosaldina, Coristina e Semavy, teve receita líquida de R$2,44 bilhões de julho ao final de setembro, alta de 9,4% sobre o mesmo período do ano passado. A média de previsões de analistas compilada pela LSEG indicava faturamento no terceiro trimestre de R$2,4 bilhões.

item.title: Fourth-tier Fleetwood stun Arsenal in League Cup shootout
item.description: Fourth-tier Fleetwood Town beat 10-man Arsenal 5-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw in the League Cup last 16 on Tuesday, pulling off a major upset at Highbury Stadium.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Fourth-tier Fleetwood Town beat 10-man Arsenal 5-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw in the League Cup last 16 on Tuesday, pulling off a major upset at Highbury Stadium. Aaron Loupalo-Bi put the League Two side ahead in the 21st minute, shrugging off Arsenal defender Marli Salmon before driving a tight-angle effort beyond goalkeeper Illan Meslier. The match had been interrupted early on for more than eight minutes after a drone was spotted above the stadium. Arsenal drew level four minutes after the break through Viktor Gyokeres, who converted from close range after Ceadach O'Neill, making his senior debut, controlled a long ball from Piero Hincapie and delivered into the area. Arsenal's task became tougher when teenager Max Dowman was sent off following an altercation with Fleetwood's Neal near the halfway line. Fleetwood weathered late Arsenal pressure, with Lynch making an important save from Ben White to take the tie to penalties. Lynch then dived to his left to palm away Guimaraes' spot-kick to put his side ahead 4-3, before Conor Haughey sent Meslier the wrong way to fire his side into the quarter-finals. "Amazing for the club, the town. Honestly it means everything to everyone," Lynch told Sky adding they took inspiration from Grimsby Town's cup victory over Manchester United last season. "We took heart from Grimsby beating Man Utd last year. We kind of compared it. The whole team throughout the game was magnificent. To beat the English champions - credit to these lads." The victory was a remarkable result for Fleetwood, who sit in the bottom half of League Two and had won only one of their previous eight league matches. In contrast, Arsenal had won seven of their opening eight Premier League games and were also unbeaten in the Champions League. Fleetwood will discover their quarter-final opponents when the League Cup draw is made after the remaining fourth-round ties on Wednesday.

item.title: Trump administration sued over rollback of corporate ownership reporting rules
item.description: Twenty-one US states and the District of Columbia sued President Donald Trump's administration on Tuesday over its rollback of reporting requirements established under a 2021 law aimed at combating illicit finance.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: Twenty-one US states and the District of Columbia sued President Donald Trump's administration on Tuesday over its [USN:L1N448124 TEXT:"rollback"] of reporting requirements established under a 2021 law aimed at combating illicit finance. The Trump administration in August [USN:L1N448124 TEXT:"finalized a rule"] exempting US companies and individuals from reporting beneficial ownership information to the Treasury Department's financial crimes unit, rolling back reporting requirements established under the 2021 Corporate Transparency Act. In their lawsuit, the coalition of mostly Democratic-led states asked a federal court to overturn the rule, which was part of a broader push by the Trump administration to curtail anti-corruption efforts. "The executive branch cannot repeal a law by rulemaking. That fundamental principle resolves this case," said the lawsuit filed in the US District Court for the District of Oregon. The lawsuit said that the Trump administration effectively gutted the 2021 law by exempting more than 99.9% of companies originally required to disclose information about their owners. The suit was filed against US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, the Department of the Treasury and its anti-money laundering Financial Crimes Enforcement Network. The Treasury Department did not respond to a request for comment. Bessent had cast the rule when it was made in August as "eliminating a burdensome reporting requirement for millions of law-abiding business owners without compromising our national security." The lawsuit also listed the heads of the US Departments of Justice and Homeland Security as defendants. "The Trump administration has effectively overturned this law by enacting a rule that exempts all domestic companies and US owners of foreign companies from the law's requirements, allowing the true owners of both foreign and domestic shell companies to remain anonymous," New York Attorney General Letitia James, who was among the more than 20 state attorneys general who filed the challenge, said in a statement. US Senator Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts, the top Democrat on the Senate Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs Committee, said in August that rolling back the reporting requirements increased the risks of sanctions evasion, fraud and drug trafficking, as well as sex trafficking and organized criminal activity.

item.title: Ministério da Agricultura confirma novo foco da doença de Newcastle em Santa Catarina
item.description: O Ministério da Agricultura e Pecuária informou nesta terça-feira que foi identificado um novo foco da doença de Newcastle em um estabelecimento avícola no município de Nova Erechim (SC).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O Ministério da Agricultura e Pecuária informou nesta terça-feira que foi identificado um novo foco da doença de Newcastle em um estabelecimento avícola no município de Nova Erechim (SC). Segundo o ministério, o foco foi identificado dentro da área de emergência sanitária estabelecida na região. O Serviço Veterinário Oficial (SVO) já iniciou as medidas previstas nos protocolos de resposta a emergências zoossanitárias, incluindo investigação epidemiológica, vigilância e contenção da doença", disse o ministério em comunicado.

item.title: After nods to rest and recovery, Pacers set to face 76ers
item.description: Two teams that have prioritized player health early in the season should be well rested and potentially near full strength when the Philadelphia 76ers visit the Indiana Pacers on Wednesday night in Indianapolis.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Two teams that have prioritized player health early in the season should be well rested and potentially near full strength when the Philadelphia 76ers visit the Indiana Pacers on Wednesday night in Indianapolis. Both teams are coming off losses in the second game of back-to-backs when they opted to give key players a night off. In the 76ers' case, those players were oft-injured center Joel Embiid and starting guard VJ Edgecombe, both of whom watched the team's first loss of the season Sunday, 106-93 at home to the Detroit Pistons. Embiid, who played a total of just 96 games over the previous three seasons, put up a triple-double with 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists in 36 minutes one night earlier as the host 76ers beat the Milwaukee Bucks 127-116. The 32-year-old averaged 34.3 minutes in Philadelphia's first three games. He followed up the loss to Milwaukee with an unusual plea to surrounding reporters. "I actually want to play (against the Pistons), so can you guys put pressure on them?" he said in a playful exchange. "I want to play (back-to-backs), so start writing articles and put pressure on them so they'll let me play." That wish was denied because of plantar fasciitis injury management, but Embiid is expected to return against the Pacers, as is Edgecombe, who was kept out against Detroit because of a bruised abdomen that occurred in the victory against Milwaukee. The second-year guard returned to practice Tuesday, and neither player appeared on the injury report. The Pacers have their own players who have taken a similar path to the matchup. Guard Andrew Nembhard and center Ivica Zubac were given the night off Monday when Indiana lost 110-102 at Milwaukee. Each player was active one night earlier when the Pacers rolled to a 136-109 win at Brooklyn, although Zubac left that game early with a sore left ankle and Nembhard was limited to 30 minutes with nagging back pain. Nembhard is expected to return against the 76ers and is questionable on the injury report, but Zubac was ruled out. "Zubac is doing better," Pacers coach Rick Carlisle said. "No timetable, but encouraging." The Pacers have placed no such limitations so far on star guard Tyrese Haliburton, who is returning from an Achilles injury that kept him out all of last season. Haliburton has played at least 31 minutes in all four of Indiana's games, scoring 18 or more points in each while recording a pair of points/assists double-doubles. The Pacers will see the 76ers' new look for the first time and will have to come up with a plan to slow veterans LeBron James and Jaylen Brown. James got a rest Saturday in the win over Milwaukee, then scored 18 points in 33 minutes Sunday against Detroit. Pacers fans know all about the two new 76ers stars. James-led teams in Miami and Cleveland eliminated the Pacers in the playoffs five times between 2012 and 2018, while Brown's Boston clubs ended Indiana's seasons in 2019 and 2024. James and Brown have a combined 35 wins -- none as teammates -- at Indiana in their NBA careers across the regular season and playoffs. --Field Level Media

item.title: Ukraine's Zelenskiy says territory recaptured, forces on the offensive
item.description: President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Tuesday that Ukrainian forces were retaking territory through a series of offensives, including one operation previously unannounced in which Kyiv's troops used gas pipelines to outflank Russian positions.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Tuesday that Ukrainian forces were retaking territory through a series of offensives, including one operation previously unannounced in which Kyiv's troops used gas pipelines to outflank Russian positions. Zelenskiy, speaking in his nightly video address, said Kyiv's battlefield position was the strongest in some time in the 4-1/2-year-long war and could be made stronger with more deliveries of air defence systems from its Western allies. Zelenskiy, citing a report by senior commanders, noted for the first time the "Veles" operation using pipelines in Ukraine's northeast. He also referred to an air assault operation in eastern Ukraine and the "Vivaldi" operation further to the north, designed to prevent Russian advances in key areas. He said Operation Veles was conducted near Kupiansk, a city in northeastern Kharkiv region recaptured by Ukrainian forces in late 2022, but since under constant Russian pressure. "It is a strong operation, well planned and technology-driven. The Russians tried to use underground gas pipelines to advance past our positions," Zelenskiy said. "Our fighters turned this tactic against the Russians and used the underground infrastructure against the occupiers with extraordinary success," he said. In the Vivaldi offensive, one senior commander [USN:L8N4570DL TEXT:"reported"] last month that Ukraine's Third Army Corps had cleared an area of 75 square kilometres (29 square miles) of Russian infiltration groups and recaptured a further 10 square kilometres. That operation was focused to the north of the key strongholds in the region — the so-called "fortress belt" of the cities Sloviansk and Kramatorsk. Their capture would bring Russia closer to its goal of seizing the entire Donbas region. Zelenskiy in August spoke of success in an offensive further south, with 26 villages being returned to Ukrainian control. Russia says it favours an overall resolution of the war rather than a short-lived ceasefire and has pledged to pursue its drive to capture all of Donbas. Russian commanders repeatedly say, often in announcements in President Vladimir Putin's presence, that their forces are advancing on all sections of the 1,200-km (750-mile) front line. The chief of Russia's General Staff, Valery Gerasimov, said this month that Moscow's forces had captured 92 Ukrainian settlements, including the town of Dobropillia, since the beginning of September. Ukraine's military [USN:S8N42201I TEXT:"dismissed"] the Russian statements.

item.title: Reports: Malik Beasley to plead guilty in federal betting case
item.description: Veteran guard Malik Beasley will enter a guilty plea in his federal betting-related bribery and conspiracy case, Beasley's attorney, Steve Haney, told multiple media outlets Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Veteran guard Malik Beasley will enter a guilty plea in his federal betting-related bribery and conspiracy case, Beasley's attorney, Steve Haney, told multiple media outlets Tuesday. Haney told ESPN and The Athletic that Beasley will plead guilty on Dec. 9 for his role in a scheme related to his play on the court. The U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of New York alleges that Beasley deliberately manipulated his statistics in certain categories in at least four games to benefit gamblers while he was playing for the Milwaukee Bucks in the 2023-24 season. Beasley, who played for six teams in nine seasons in the NBA from 2016-25, was indicted on federal charges in June. He initially pleaded not guilty to all counts. Beasley was charged with bribery in sporting contests, wire fraud conspiracy, honest services wire fraud conspiracy and money laundering conspiracy. The indictment alleges that Beasley lost millions of dollars gambling during his career and agreed to adjust his performance so his alleged co-conspirators could wager on his statistics. Beasley, a first-round pick in the 2016 NBA Draft by the Denver Nuggets, made nearly $60 million in his NBA career. He averaged 11.7 points in 578 games with the Nuggets, Minnesota Timberwolves, Utah Jazz, Los Angeles Lakers, Bucks and Detroit Pistons. Former NBA player Ed Davis also was charged in the case and has pleaded not guilty. --Field Level Media

item.title: German taxi operator MTZ to deploy up to 500 autonomous taxis under Tensor deal
item.description: Germany's largest taxi operator Münchner-Taxi-Zentrum (MTZ) and US autonomous-driving company Tensor Auto signed on Tuesday a letter of intent to deploy self-driving taxis in Germany as taxi operators seek a bigger role in Europe's emerging autonomous-mobility market.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Germany's largest taxi operator Münchner-Taxi-Zentrum (MTZ) and US autonomous-driving company Tensor Auto signed on Tuesday a letter of intent to deploy self-driving taxis in Germany as taxi operators seek a bigger role in Europe's emerging autonomous-mobility market. The companies said MTZ would operate up to 500 autonomous vehicles in German cities under its own brand, while Tensor would provide autonomous-driving technology through a subscription model. California-based Tensor's model would see taxi operators retain control of fleet operations, customer relationships and operational data rather than the technology provider running the service The autonomous vehicles would be integrated into MTZ's existing dispatch platform, allowing passengers to book rides through current taxi channels The companies said they aim to expand the model across Europe, with a target deployment of 10,000 additional vehicles through taxi and fleet operators within 24 months of the vehicle becoming available in the region MTZ and Tensor, founded in 2016 by Jay Xiao, will also explore offering the autonomous vehicles to private buyers in Germany No financial terms were disclosed, and the agreement remains contingent on Germany granting Level 4 autonomous-driving approvals Waymo said this month it was planning to launch a fully autonomous ride-hailing service [USN:L8N46613L TEXT:"in Madrid"] in 2027, as autonomous-taxi companies expand in Europe

item.title: FMI dice alcanza acuerdo a nivel técnico con Argentina en tercera revisión de programa
item.description: El Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI) y Argentina alcanzaron el martes un acuerdo a nivel técnico que podría permitir a Argentina acceder a unos 900 millones de dólares, informó el organismo desde Washington.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI) y Argentina alcanzaron el martes un acuerdo a nivel técnico que podría permitir a Argentina acceder a unos 900 millones de dólares, informó el organismo desde Washington. El FMI señaló que, antes de que la revisión sea sometida a su Directorio Ejecutivo a principios de diciembre, es necesario completar los "pasos acordados restantes", aunque no mencionó ninguna "medida previa". El acuerdo permitiría el desembolso de 900 millones de dólares, informó en su página web. "Las políticas macroeconómicas disciplinadas y las reformas orientadas al mercado continúan respaldando el proceso de desinflación y las mejoras de la posición externa de Argentina, y la acumulación de reservas supera los compromisos asumidos en el marco del programa" sostuvo el FMI en un comunicado. Las reservas internacionales netas de Argentina superaron el objetivo fijado en el programa para finales de junio, gracias a las importantes compras de divisas realizadas por el banco central, indicó el organismo. El FMI señaló que el Tesoro y el banco central de Argentina tomaron medidas para fortalecer el financiamiento externo y extender los plazos de vencimiento de la deuda. El gobierno del presidente Javier Milei ha obtenido financiamiento externo adicional y busca conseguir más fondos antes de que finalice el año, añadió el Fondo. El acuerdo se produce tras meses de conversaciones entre Argentina y el FMI, que había destacado anteriormente la necesidad de seguir recomponiendo las reservas, reducir los riesgos de financiamiento y preservar el ancla fiscal.

item.title: Espanyol sack Gonzalez following shock Sestao defeat
item.description: Espanyol have sacked coach Manolo Gonzalez following their Copa del Rey defeat by fourth-tier Sestao River Club, the LaLiga side said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Espanyol have sacked coach Manolo Gonzalez following their Copa del Rey defeat by fourth-tier Sestao River Club, the LaLiga side said on Tuesday. Gonzalez, who admitted before the match that his future was at stake, paid the price for Espanyol's 4-3 extra-time loss to Sestao. "RCD Espanyol, on behalf of club president Alan Pace, and its Board of Directors, wish to express our gratitude to Manolo Gonzalez for the work, commitment, and effort he has shown since taking charge of the first team," Espanyol said in a statement. "The club particularly values the professionalism and dedication he brought to his role, as well as the way he tackled the various sporting challenges he faced." Appointed in March 2024, Gonzalez guided Espanyol to promotion within months of taking charge and then kept the Catalan club in LaLiga over the following two seasons. "(I'm) feeling really down, completely shattered, and bearing the full weight of responsibility for everything," Gonzalez told reporters after the defeat to Sestao. "It’s one of the worst days of my life, without a doubt." Espanyol have struggled for form in 2026, losing five of Gonzalez's final six games in charge. They are 18th in the LaLiga standings with eight points and host Villarreal on Friday.
