item.title: Wall Street cierra al alza gracias al renovado impulso de la IA
item.description: Un repunte tecnológico impulsado por la inteligencia artificial llevó a las bolsas estadounidenses a cerrar al alza el martes, a medida que la temporada de presentación de resultados del tercer trimestre cobraba impulso y mientras la Reserva Federal se reunía para celebrar su penúltima reunión del año.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Culp, Shashwat Chauhan
item.content:encoded: Un repunte tecnológico impulsado por la inteligencia artificial llevó a las bolsas estadounidenses a cerrar al alza el martes, a medida que la temporada de presentación de resultados del tercer trimestre cobraba impulso y mientras la Reserva Federal se reunía para celebrar su penúltima reunión del año. El Nasdaq, con gran presencia tecnológica, encabezó las subidas. El revuelo en torno a los detalles de la inminente salida a bolsa de Anthropic contribuyó a impulsar las acciones de las empresas de semiconductores (.SOX) por tercera sesión consecutiva. La creciente preocupación por la viabilidad del gasto financiado con deuda, en un contexto de subida de los costos de financiación, ha lastrado el sector de la IA este mes. El índice Philadelphia SE Semiconductor, aunque se sitúa más de un 20% por debajo de su máximo histórico de cierre del 22 de junio, ha superado al mercado en general este año. Para financiar su expansión en el ámbito de la IA, Meta (META.O) aumentó su mayor ronda de financiación de capital hasta la fecha a 97.500 millones de dólares, lo que provocó una caída de las acciones de la empresa matriz de Facebook. "(La noticia sobre Anthropic) parece estar provocando un pequeño repunte de alivio en las acciones del sector de la IA, especialmente en las de semiconductores", dijo Chuck Carlson, presidente ejecutivo de Horizon Investment Services, refiriéndose a las acciones de fabricantes de chips. "Esas acciones se han visto muy castigadas en las últimas semanas y probablemente ya era hora de que se recuperaran". Los datos económicos mostraron un aumento de los nuevos pedidos de computadores y equipos periféricos, lo que respalda la idea de un fuerte gasto relacionado con la IA. Se espera que Microsoft (MSFT.O) y Alphabet (GOOGL.O) publiquen sus resultados el miércoles, mientras que Amazon.com lo hará el jueves. La Fed se reunió el martes para celebrar su reunión de política monetaria de octubre, de la que se espera ampliamente que culmine con la decisión de mantener sin cambios la tasa de interés objetivo de los fondos federales en el rango del 3,75% al 4%, reservando su segunda subida de tasas del año para su última reunión en diciembre, según la herramienta FedWatch de CME. "Parece haber más confianza en que la Fed no va a tomar ninguna medida en esta reunión, en parte porque el martes hay elecciones", añadió Carlson. "Probablemente haya al menos cierto alivio al saber que la situación de las tasas no va a obstaculizar un repunte". Según datos preliminares, el S&P 500 (.SPX) subió 46,28 puntos, o un 0,60%, a 7.723,05 unidades, mientras que el Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) ganó 309,69 puntos, o un 1,18%, a 26.479,08. El Promedio Industrial Dow Jones (.DJI) avanzó 25,60 puntos, o un 0,05%, a 52.387,18 unidades.

item.title: Lula's win in Brazil deals harsh blow to Trump’s ‘Donroe Doctrine’: McGeever
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's surprise reelection victory on Sunday dealt a harsh blow to US President Donald Trump’s Donroe Doctrine, a plan to secure a US "sphere of influence" in the Americas against growing Chinese influence. The question now is just how much Brazil will tilt toward Beijing.
item.dc:creator: Jamie McGeever
item.content:encoded: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's [USN:L6N4681ER TEXT:"surprise reelection victory"] on Sunday dealt a harsh blow to US President Donald Trump’s [USN:L1N43A0RG TEXT:""Donroe Doctrine,""] a plan to secure a US "sphere of influence" in the Americas against growing Chinese influence. The question now is just how much Brazil will tilt toward Beijing. Trump's grand plans at the start of the year to solidify Washington's influence over Latin America were epitomized by US forces' extraordinary [USN:L6N3Y407K TEXT:"capture and extradition"] of Venezuela's leftist President Nicolas Maduro on January 3. Lula's victory has thrown a spanner in the works. South America's most populous nation will be led for another four years by the [USN:L6N46B06R TEXT:"veteran leftist"] and long-standing critic of US influence. Trump [USN:L6N46C02Y TEXT:"said on Monday"] that he likes Lula and gets along well with him, but it's safe to say he would have had a more cordial relationship with Lula’s right-wing opponent, Flavio Bolsonaro, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro. What makes Lula's win even more vexing for Washington is that it is likely to strengthen Brazil's ties with China, a process that Lula has long championed. China overtook the US as Brazil's largest trading partner in 2009. Officially, Lula will avoid aligning himself too closely with either superpower. "We are no one's backyard!" Lula told thousands of supporters at his victory rally in Sao Paulo on Sunday. That could be interpreted as a warning to the US and China that Brazil will not be bullied into relinquishing control of its vast resources, from energy and minerals to the Amazon rainforest. But "backyard" clearly sounds like a nod to the US. Trump's "Donroe Doctrine," a revival of the 200-year-old "Monroe Doctrine" that claimed the US should have a "zone of influence" in the Americas, has not been particularly well received in Latin America. A victory for Trump's political ally Flavio Bolsonaro on Sunday would likely have strengthened Washington's plans in the region, which may have pushed other countries to trim ties with Beijing. But with Lula's continued tenure, the White House may need to focus more on damage control. "Lula’s victory certainly reinforces Brazil’s economic relationship with China," says Emanuel Ornelas, a professor at the Sao Paulo School of Economics-FGV. For a White House intent on expanding US influence at China’s expense, that is worrisome. CHINA’S GROWING FOOTPRINT As the battle between the US and China for global economic supremacy ratchets up amid an escalating AI arms race, securing a reliable supply of energy, resources and materials has become more important than ever. Brazil sits across all of those areas. Brazil holds around 20% of global rare earth reserves and is a major producer of a range of minerals critical to technologies like semiconductors, renewable energy, robotics and defense applications. Its resources are a key part of global supply chains, and the country is also an agricultural powerhouse, supplying the world with around 27% of its sugarcane, 25% of its soybeans, 9% of its cotton, and 6% of its beef and corn. China already has a distinct advantage. Brazil currently exports around three times as much to China as it does to the US, in dollar terms, and imports around twice as much from the Asian superpower as it does from America. This gap is widening. Trump's tariffs pushed China to increasingly replace US agricultural goods with Brazilian alternatives. The war in the Middle East has also tightened trade ties between Brasilia and Beijing by disrupting normal energy trade patterns. Crude oil now rivals soybeans as Brazil’s largest export and has helped fill the gap created by shuttered Middle East production. China is the largest buyer of both. While Brazil plays a multifaceted role in US plans to remain the world’s main superpower, China's view of Brazil appears more straightforward. It wants access to the commodities, energy and minerals needed to sustain its industrial base, which increasingly includes high-value manufacturing. Will Lula have a strong enough hand to secure advantageous terms with the US and China as they seek access to Brazil's resources? This could prove challenging. He faces many hurdles at home, including a high likelihood of legislative gridlock in Brasilia. Markets don't seem enthused either. While the [USN:L6N46C031 TEXT:"historic plunge"] in Brazilian markets (.BVSP) , on Monday following Lula's win was exaggerated, it was telling nonetheless: investors appear very skeptical about the country's fiscal outlook and economic growth prospects. What happens matters beyond the country’s borders. Brazil, in UniCredit’s words, is both a "strategic resource power" and a "geopolitical swing state" in the US-China rivalry. Which side will prevail? That remains a toss-up. (The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters) Enjoying this column? item.title: Court orders Egyptian website closed in case seen as test for independent media
item.description: An Egyptian court convicted the editor-in-chief of leading independent news website Mada Masr of running it without a licence on Tuesday, ordered the site closed and held her in custody for five hours, her lawyers and the outlet said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: An Egyptian court convicted the editor-in-chief of leading independent news website Mada Masr of running it without a licence on Tuesday, ordered the site closed and held her in custody for five hours, her lawyers and the outlet said. Lina Attalah of the online newspaper Mada Masr, which has won numerous international awards for its reporting, was fined 3 million Egyptian pounds ($53,400), her lawyers told Reuters. She was released after Mada Masr paid the fine, the newspaper said. The ruling targets the most internationally prominent independent outlet in a media landscape mostly dominated by the state, and it comes a month after authorities [USN:L6N45M11C TEXT:"arrested the entire newsroom"] of the fact-checking outlet Matsaddash. Rights groups have criticized the case against Attalah. Mada Masr, which was founded in 2013, regularly publishes stories on politically sensitive topics. Her lawyers said the court rejected their requests during Tuesday's session to review the case file and submit additional evidence and instead issued her a court-appointed lawyer despite her objection. State authorities did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The court gave her the maximum penalty, ordering the website to be shut down and its equipment confiscated, Mada Masr said in a statement. The independent outlet said in a separate statement that during release procedures, Attalah was informed of a one-year prison term handed to her in absentia in 2024 on charges of disseminating false news and managing an unlicensed website. It said a retrial of the separate case was set for November 11 after her lawyers took steps to challenge the 2024 ruling. Prosecutors referred Attalah to trial last Thursday. A group of 119 rights groups and media outlets, including Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch and the Committee to Protect Journalists, called the case an "unprecedented attack on press freedom." US Senator Chris Van Hollen, a Maryland Democrat, said in a statement on the social media platform X on Friday that the charges were baseless and that "journalism is not a crime." Egyptian authorities say the state is committed to upholding freedom of expression but that the media must operate within the law, respect national security and counter misinformation. YEARS OF LEGAL BATTLES Egyptian authorities have blocked Mada Masr inside the country since 2017. Mada Masr says six cases have been brought against it and its journalists over the last six years, though rights groups say this is the first of its kind to be referred to trial. Attalah was named one of the world's 100 most influential people by Time magazine in 2020. Mada Masr says it has asked for a licence from the Supreme Council for Media Regulation repeatedly since 2018 but heard nothing back and learned of a rejection only when prosecutors raised the issue during an earlier case in 2022. The outlet contested that decision in court and said its latest application has been awaiting a response since 2023. The council has not commented on the case but has said that it facilitates procedures for outlets that meet official requirements and is keen to promote freedom of expression. In September, the US [USN:L1N45N19B TEXT:"waived rights conditions"], which include protecting media freedoms, on a portion of the roughly $1.3 billion of military aid it sends Egypt each year.

item.title: Artiva to discontinue cell therapy after two patient deaths, cut workforce by 94%
item.description: Artiva Biotherapeutics said on Tuesday it would halt the development of an experimental cell therapy for certain autoimmune conditions — its lead candidate — after two patient deaths, sending its shares slumping 32%.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Artiva Biotherapeutics (ARTV.O) said on Tuesday it would halt the development of an experimental cell therapy for certain autoimmune conditions — its lead candidate — after two patient deaths, sending its shares slumping 32%. The company will slash its workforce by about 94% and evaluate strategic alternatives, it said. Here are more details: Artiva's therapy AlloNK was being tested as a potential treatment for autoimmune conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis in a mid-stage trial The company said one of the patients in the trial experienced a fatal neurological event following treatment The investigator and an independent safety review assessed the event as likely related to complications caused by the chemotherapy drug fludarabine, the company said A second patient in the trial experienced sudden death about two months after initiating treatment, which an investigator assessed as unrelated to AlloNK, Artiva added "Two patient deaths plus fading durability quickly transformed what looked like a promising and differentiated path forward into one that carried too much risk and uncertainty," said Cantor Fitzgerald analyst Josh Schimmer Schimmer said a path forward with AlloNK would have been a challenging one with an incredibly high cost of capital As of September 30, Artiva had about $319.1 million in cash, cash equivalents and investments As of December 31, 2025, the company had 104 full-time employees, according to its annual filing

item.title: TSX hits six-day high, led by Celestica and metal miners
item.description: Canada's main stock index rose to a six-day high on Tuesday as Celestica's quarterly results impressed investors and higher gold prices gave metal mining shares a boost.
item.dc:creator: Fergal Smith
item.content:encoded: Canada's main stock index rose to a six-day high on Tuesday as Celestica's quarterly results impressed investors and higher gold prices gave metal mining shares a boost. The S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) ended up 227.33 points, or 0.6%, at 36,171.49, notching its highest closing level since last Wednesday. [USN:L6N46D1C7 TEXT:"US stocks"] also ended higher, helped by an AI-fueled tech rally. "Overall, upbeat across North American markets," said Michael Dehal, a senior portfolio manager at Dehal Investment Partners at Raymond James. "We got great results from Celestica last night so that's giving a boost to our tech sector in Canada," Dehal said. "We're getting more optimism around the AI trade in the US." Shares of [USN:L2N46C109 TEXT:"Celestica"] (CLS.TO) jumped 11.9% after the electronic equipment company's quarterly results beat estimates, contributing to a 0.7% gain for technology (.SPTTTK) . The materials sector (.GSPTTMT) , which includes metal mining shares, was up 3.3%. Gold rose 1.1% as lower oil prices lent support, with market participants awaiting the Federal Reserve's policy decision on Wednesday for signals on the future path of US interest rates. The [USN:L6N46915P TEXT:"Bank of Canada's"] latest interest rate decision is also due on Wednesday, with investors expecting the first rate hike since July 2023. Both industrials (.GSPTTIN) and heavily weighted financials were up 0.7%. Four of the 10 major sectors ended lower, including energy, which lost 2.6%. [USN:L2N46D00J TEXT:"U.S. crude oil futures"] settled down 1.8% at $99.90 a barrel as traders focused on Middle East peace talks. Canada and the United Arab Emirates signed a [USN:L6N46D14J TEXT:"comprehensive trade deal"] to lower barriers between the two economies and boost investment, the governments said, as Prime Minister Mark Carney seeks to expand trade and investment ties at a time of tension with the US.
